thesis: Embeddings and input-dependent attention let text prediction build rich representations, while generation still optimizes plausible continuation.
role: Explain language models and retrieval without equating fluency with truth.

ideas.statement: Embeddings map related content near one another; attention creates contextual representations through query-key matching and weighted values.
A language model predicts tokens through lookup, Transformer blocks, a vocabulary distribution and repeated sampling; pretraining, instruction examples and preference feedback serve different roles.
Retrieval supplies relevant documents before answering; chunking, exact-match search, reranking and separate retrieval/answer evaluation matter.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Two senses of bank illustrate context; an invented API method illustrates fluent hallucination.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Embedding maps carry prejudices, and attention maps are clues rather than full explanations.

audit.notes: Entire assigned segment reviewed; scope and qualifications preserved. Duplicate contents and publication metadata are not ranked as ideas.
